policy: Scenario exceptions, then Fifth Edition rules, then annex class and dated refit entries. Legacy dated Form 10 is corroboration, with differences retained explicitly. Nulls and unresolved alternatives are not executable; printed conflicts are retained verbatim and marked.

scenario_source.note: PDF 65 (printed 64) contains the complete 'Battle of Cape Esperance' scenario text. Adjacent pages checked: PDF 64 (printed 63) starts 'Missed Opportunity', PDF 66 (printed 65) starts 'Guadalcanal Air Battle'. The scenario page carries no chart; setup is relative placements on open ocean.

registered_record.verification: The registered page numbers (PDF 65, printed 64) match the actual PDF. The registered start time, environment, rosters, deployment, three start options, victory conditions and special rules were re-verified against the page; additions and corrections in this package are listed in conflicts and pending_items.

visual_detection.convention: Clear Night visibility is modified by the moon phase; the scenario provides 10% visibility directly. Gun flashes raise visibility by tables per the Visibility Modifiers Table (printed 5-14, PDF 51).

scenario_relevant_rows: 20mm - 74mm gun flashes increase visibility at night by two tables/rows, up to 70% visibility.
75mm and larger gunfire flashes or rocket-propelled weapons increase visibility at night by three tables/rows, up to 70% visibility.
A cued visual search (knowing where to look): -20% (detection roll modifier; the 2345 reaction-fire rule explicitly allows a cued visual search).
Ships firing in 20% or 10% visibility (unmodified) reduces their visual detection chances by -20%.

squalls.movement: circles move at wind speed and direction

nighttime_illumination.convention: Searchlight max illumination range halved at 10% (night precip) to 5% visibility, 25% at 2%; starshell and flare ranges halved at 10-5% and completely ineffective at 2%.
nighttime_illumination.scenario_illumination_events: none printed on the scenario page

environment.squalls_text: Heavy rain squalls 5 to 50 nmi northwest of Savo Island

us_formation.column_text: Steaming in column on course 045 deg, speed 15 knots. Farenholt, Duncan, and Laffey are in the lead, then cruisers San Francisco, Boise, Salt Lake City, Helena. The destroyers Buchanan and McCalla are in the rear.

scheduled_course_reversal.text: As previously planned, Scott ordered the column to reverse course at 2330. The Japanese formation was closing at right angles at 30 knots, still immersed in a squall.
scheduled_course_reversal.note: printed in the Setup narrative; applies to the 23:24 start, not reprinted as a table row

us_formation.radar_note: Helena's SG radar had greater range than that on the flagship, and poor communications procedures prevented Helena's information from reaching Admiral Scott.

japan_formation.column_text: The three Japanese cruisers are in column, Aoba in front, followed by Furutaka and Kinugasa.

screen.note: the beam references are relative to Aoba, not to the column ends

japan_formation.floatplane_state: All cruisers carry half of their rated floatplane capacity.

start_options.text: Historical positions as printed in Setup; the page gives no special fire phase for this start.
start_options.japanese_detection: not stated for 23:24; the Special Rules keep the Japanese unaware until gun flashes are spotted at close range

enemy_from_helena.unit_note: printed as 'six miles'; the page does not specify nautical miles (see conflicts helena-radio-range-unit)

start_options.text: After ten minutes, Helena's captain radioed Scott that the Japanese force was now six miles away, bearing 285 deg. If the players wish, they may use that position as the starting point for the battle.
start_options.japanese_detection: At this time (use 2339) the Japanese had not detected the American force.

start_options.text: At 2345 Helena radioed that she had Japanese ships in sight bearing 300 deg at 5000 yards, and opened fire after another set of crossed signals.
start_options.fire_rule: Helena is allowed to fire in the Planned Fire Phase of turn 2345, and the rest of the American force in the reaction fire phase, if they successfully detect the Japanese (cued visual search or radar).
start_options.japanese_detection: The Japanese had still not detected the Americans.

victory_conditions_as_printed.independence_note: the page gives each side its own conditions and no rule makes one side's achievement cancel the other's; both sides can satisfy their conditions in the same battle and the results are kept separately

special_rules_as_printed.surprise_fire: The Japanese were unaware of the presence of the American force until their gun flashes were spotted at close range. The Americans get one free Tactical Turn of fire before the Japanese can return fire.
special_rules_as_printed.cease_fire_d10: Each side must roll D10 once every Tactical Turn. If the D10 roll is 1, the ships of that side must cease fire for one Tactical Turn. The pause only occurs once for each side during the battle. Cease rolling after it occurs.
special_rules_as_printed.helena_2345_fire_rule: At the 2345 start, Helena may fire in the Planned Fire Phase of turn 2345; the rest of the American force fires in the reaction fire phase only if they successfully detect the Japanese (cued visual search or radar).
special_rules_as_printed.bombardment_duration: Japanese orders: shell Henderson Field for 90 minutes (30 Tactical Turns); the page equates 90 minutes with 30 Tactical Turns but prints no per-turn duration

conflicts.detail: A-13 class fit '2F/A(3)3 Mk12, 15 8in/55' plus the remark 'First three units had Mk9 or Mk14 8in/55 guns' (New Orleans, Astoria, Minneapolis) implies Mk12/15 for San Francisco (Annex C-2 row). San Francisco's own Mar 42 Form 10 (page 245) prints 'Fwd (3)/Fwd (3)/Aft (3) Mk9/14 8 in/55', and its APC row (33/25, 22/19, 15/5/16) tracks the C-3 Mk9/14 ranges and pens with +1/+1/+1 damage over the C-3 values. Both readings are registered; the row selection stays with the runtime consumer and shells must not be spliced.

The 2339 option prints 'six miles away, bearing 285'. The page does not state nautical vs statute miles; the 23:24 deployment and the chart-less setup otherwise use nautical miles (13.5 nmi). The registered record data/campaign/cape-esperance.json reads it as 6 nmi. Kept as printed with the unit ambiguity noted.

Annex A-14 Furutaka (1937) prints '(4 reserve torp/mount for quick reload in 6 minutes)'; the Dec 1941 Form 10 (page 53) shows the two quad mounts with 4 torpedoes each and no reload boxes. Whether Furutaka carried reloads on 1942-10-11 is not resolved by these sources; the annex value is registered in the profile with the form difference retained.

Annex A-14 Furutaka (1937) Light AA prints '(2)4 Type 96 25mm, (2)2 Type 93 13.2mm (1.2)'; the Dec 1941 Form 10 prints '4 13.2mm' only (0.2). The 25mm fit date is not printed in either source beyond the 1937 block placement; both prints are retained.

A-14 remark 'Oct 42: E7K2 Alf floatplanes replaced by E13A1 Jake' is dated by month only, against the 11 Oct 42 battle; the Dec 1941 Form 10 lists 2 E7K1. Aircraft type and the exact half-capacity rounding for Furutaka (annex rated 1; form 2 boxes) are not resolved; the scenario state stays 'half of rated capacity' as printed.

Aoba/Kinugasa Dec 1941 Form 10s print crew 657-680 and signature Medium/Loud; the annex prints crew 625 and Medium/Noisy. Furutaka's form prints Medium/Loud against the annex Medium/Noisy. The annex values are registered in the profiles; the form differences are retained and not adjudicated.

Fubuki (Apr-May 42) and Hatsuyuki (Dec 1941) Form 10s print 139 DP with speed rows 0/35/70/104/125/139; the Annex A-27 1936-refit row is 106 DP with 0/27/53/80/95/106. Cross-references the fubuki-damage conflict in cape-st-george-1943.json; the annex row remains the registered profile.

The Boise (265) and Helena (263) forms print 6in/47 APC short-range values (pen 20, dam 22) higher than the registered Annex C-2 Mk16 row (pen 15, dam 18), and the Bristol/Cruiser US forms similarly run +1/+2 over the annex damage at short range. Per the fletcher-gun-table convention in cape-st-george-1943.json, the matched Annex C rows control and form values are retained as corroboration, not spliced.

The registered record data/campaign/cape-esperance.json omits the 2330 scheduled US course reversal, the SOC-3 availability narrative (4 available, 2 launched by San Francisco and Boise, 1 aborted, 1 lost in a launch mishap, 1 jettisoned), the squall-immersion note at contact, and the Japanese-vs-US 'damage ratio'/'damage point ratio' wording difference. All are added here as printed. The registered start/deployment/environment/victory data itself re-verified without discrepancy.
